summary: GPL Tokenizer (~6k LOC Python, /Users/limit/Projects/gpl-tokenizer) is a geometry-aware SVG tokenization pipeline: parser/ (PathParser regex-parses path d-strings with relative->absolute resolution and S/T smooth-command promotion at path_parser.py:256-307; SVGParser normalizes circle/rect/ellipse/line/poly* into path commands, circles become 4 cubic Beziers with kappa=0.5522847498 at svg_parser.py:322-347). analyzer/ computes sampled Bezier curvature profiles (curvature.py), G0/G1/G2 joint continuity against thresholds centralized in utils/constants.py (GeometricConstants dataclass), pattern-matched shape detection (M+4C+Z -> circle/ellipse, M+3-4L+Z -> rect; shape_detector.py:142-360), and multi-element spatial relations via pixel-tolerance grouping (alignment/equal-spacing/symmetry/equal-size, spatial_analyzer.py). The ARCS coordinate system (tokenizer/arcs.py) is a quadtree over a square canvas: a complexity grid at 2^max_level resolution accumulates curvature x arc-length over segment endpoint bboxes (arcs.py:116-149), nodes split where complexity > 0.5 down to max_level=6 (64x64), else stop at min_level=2 (4x4, 75px cells); quantize() finds the containing leaf and emits (level, qx, qy) on a global per-level grid; dequantize() returns the cell center, giving an analytic error bound of (cell_size/2)*sqrt(2) (arcs.py:252-266). Vocabulary (vocabulary.py) is a fixed 5,561-token layout: IDs 0-99 structural (special/command/composite/continuity/16 curvature bins/spatial) plus 5,461 coordinate tokens (sum of 4^l, l=0..6) from ID 100. L1 (primitive_tokenizer.py) emits [CMD][coord...][continuity][curvature-bin] per command; L2 (composite_tokenizer.py) replaces detected shape spans with [CIRCLE][center][radius-as-coord] etc.; L3 (spatial_tokenizer.py) encodes one anchor element plus EQUAL_SIZE/ALIGN/EQUAL_SPACE/REPEAT_k relation tokens, encoding scalar spacing/axis/repeat-count by pushing (v,v) through the 2D position quantizer (spatial_tokenizer.py:382-401). The detokenizer (detokenizer.py) reverses tokens to path d-strings or full SVG documents, reconstructing spatial groups by translating/mirroring previously emitted elements, and ships v0.5.1 fidelity-measurement APIs (extract_coordinates, measure_fidelity). All 6 test scripts I ran pass (113 assertions), and README/RESEARCH_SUMMARY claim 2-3x GID gain over BPE, 5.6x circle compression "with zero information loss," up to 15x vs BPE, and a 19x quantization-error improvement from adaptive refinement. Empirical probing shows the headline lossless claim is false at the value level (see weaknesses).
strengths: Quantization error is treated analytically, not just empirically: theoretical_max_error derives the correct (cell_size/2)*sqrt(2) bound and roundtrip_fidelity/measure_fidelity verify max/mean/RMS error against it (arcs.py:252-311, detokenizer.py:82-156), with tests confirming the bound holds for 1000 random points and canvas-corner edge cases (tests/test_fidelity.py:70-184).

Coordinate decoding is encoder-tree-independent: dequantize() needs only (level, qx, qy) and canvas_size (arcs.py:217-225), so a decoder never needs the encoder's adaptive quadtree — a sound design choice for LM generation.

The vocabulary layout is explicit, compact, and bijective: a documented ID map with reserved expansion ranges (vocabulary.py:106-126) and a deterministic coord<->ID table (vocabulary.py:138-153); 5,561 total matches the documented sum (100 + (4^7-1)/3).

Threshold unification is real engineering hygiene: G0/G1/G2 cutoffs that previously diverged between continuity.py and math_utils.py are now sourced from one frozen GeometricConstants dataclass with an optional relative-G2 mode to avoid over-sensitivity at near-zero curvature (utils/constants.py:27-81, continuity.py:160-168).

PathParser handles genuinely tricky SVG path semantics correctly: implicit lineto after multi-coordinate M (path_parser.py:147-162), S/T control-point reflection with promotion to C/Q (path_parser.py:256-307), scientific-notation numbers (path_parser.py:104-106).

Shape detection verifies geometry rather than only matching command patterns: circle detection cross-checks two center estimates and radius spread (shape_detector.py:188-230); rect detection enforces perpendicular adjacent edges and equal opposite sides (shape_detector.py:316-341).

The test suite is real and passing — I executed test_roundtrip (24), test_level2 (23), test_level3 (24), test_fidelity (17), test_constants (12), test_generator_validation (13), all green — and test_fidelity genuinely demonstrates the adaptive-tree error reduction (tests/test_fidelity.py:119-146).

Documentation is honest in places where projects usually oversell: hmn_init.py:50-55 explicitly concedes the 0.52 adjacent-coordinate cosine similarity is a design artifact of d_model/level/frequency choices, not a target metric, and derives it step by step.
weaknesses: The 'zero information loss' claim is false beyond element topology, including on the README's own flagship example. Reproduced: 5 circles (cx=50..250, r=20, spacing 50) tokenize to 11 L3 tokens but reconstruct as r=37.5 (87% radius error), spacing 37.5, and shifted centers. Root cause: scalar values (radius, width/height, spacing, alignment axis) are encoded by quantizing the fake 2D point (v,v) through the position quadtree (composite_tokenizer.py:165, spatial_tokenizer.py:382-389); near-origin scalars land in coarse min_level=2 cells (75px wide) and dequantize to 37.5.

REPEAT_N round-trip is catastrophically broken: the repeat count is encoded as a quantized coordinate _q(float(count), float(count)) (spatial_tokenizer.py:400-401) and decoded as int(coord[0]) (detokenizer.py:343-347). Reproduced: 7 circles in a row reconstruct as 38 circles (count 6 -> quantized to 37.5 -> 37 repeats). Tests never cover REPEAT_N — test_level3.py only counts elements for 3- and 5-circle cases (test_level3.py:292-297) and never compares reconstructed values.

decode_token_id crashes with ValueError on reserved IDs 5-9 (vocabulary.py:203-204, SpecialToken(5) raises) and 71-79 (vocabulary.py:209-210, the branch spans 60<=id<80 but SpatialToken only defines 60-70) — directly contradicting the v0.5.1 docstring claim that reserved ranges decode to 'unknown' (vocabulary.py:121-123). Verified by execution. Since a trained model samples over the full 5,561-ID softmax, generated sequences containing these IDs make Detokenizer.detokenize raise; GPLGenerator swallows this with a bare except (generator.py:160-166), silently deflating the reported 53.3% validity rate.

Arc (A) commands are heavily lossy: x-rotation, large-arc and sweep flags are discarded at tokenization (primitive_tokenizer.py:212-216 keeps only rx/ry and endpoint) and the detokenizer hardcodes '0 0 1' (detokenizer.py:638). Reproduced: 'A 60 30 45 1 0 200 150' round-trips to 'A 37.5 37.5 0 0 1 199.2 152.3' — radii also mangled because (rx,ry) is quantized as a position.

All styling is destroyed: fill/stroke/stroke-width/opacity are parsed into attributes (svg_parser.py:143-147) but never tokenized, and every reconstructed element hardcodes fill="none" stroke="black" stroke-width="1" (detokenizer.py:163-164, 194, 421-479). transform is parsed but explicitly unprocessed (svg_parser.py:24), so any transformed SVG is geometrically misinterpreted without warning.

Adaptive resolution is driven solely by curvature x arc-length, so straight-line art gets the worst resolution: zero curvature -> no refinement -> min_level=2 -> up to ~53px error on a 300px canvas. Reproduced: 'M 10 10 L 100 100' reconstructs as 'M 37.5 37.5 L 112.5 112.5'. The advertised 19x error improvement (README.md:64) only applies where curvature happens to exist; positional accuracy of lines/polygons matters just as much visually.

Tokenization is input-dependent: the quadtree is rebuilt from each element's own curvature (primitive_tokenizer.py:108-110, 225-246), so the same coordinate maps to different token IDs across inputs, and in SpatialTokenizer the shared arcs ends up being whatever tree the last element built (spatial_tokenizer.py:92-97, composite_tokenizer.py:82-84). This is a poor inductive property for a learned LM and is never ablated against uniform quantization.

Compression baselines are estimates, not measurements: 'vs BPE' is computed as len(svg_text)/4 (test_roundtrip.py:331-334), and when no original text is supplied the char count is guessed as commands*20 (primitive_tokenizer.py:128, composite_tokenizer.py:137). No real tokenizer (tiktoken, GPT-2 BPE, or the cited StrokeNUWA/IconShop token schemes) is ever run.

Shape detection is brittle and order/orientation dependent: circles/ellipses must be exactly M+4C+Z with axis-aligned extreme points (shape_detector.py:155-230) — rotated ellipses, two-arc circles, and polygon-approximated circles all fall through to L1; round-rect radius is estimated from segment endpoint deltas with hardcoded 0.85 confidence (shape_detector.py:411-446). Symmetry detection requires every element in the scene to participate (spatial_analyzer.py:249-252), and the decoder mirrors all previously emitted elements rather than the symmetric group (detokenizer.py:289-308), which duplicates unrelated elements in mixed scenes.

Dead and self-colliding code: QuantizedCoord.to_id (arcs.py:58-64) implements a second, incompatible ID scheme with no COORD_TOKEN_BASE offset — verified it returns 0 (collides with PAD) and 15 (collides with QUADRATIC) — and is referenced nowhere.

DiffAttr tokens are write-only: continuity and curvature-bin tokens are parsed by the detokenizer but never used in reconstruction (detokenizer.py:247-252, 587-591), so at L1 they purely inflate token count — which also flatters the L2 'circle 28->5 tokens = 5.6x' comparison since the 28 includes these advisory tokens.

The complexity map uses only segment endpoint bounding boxes (primitive_tokenizer.py:230-237), not Bezier control points, so curve regions bulging outside the endpoint bbox get no resolution refinement; arc curvature is approximated as 1/mean(rx,ry) with arc_length = chord*1.2 (curvature.py:193-223).
research_limits: No real-world data anywhere: every reported number derives from 7 hand-written toy SVGs (tests/test_roundtrip.py:29-49) or a synthetic generator with 7 shape/pattern types (training/synthetic_dataset.py). A publishable claim needs evaluation on standard corpora (FontAwesome, Noto Emoji, SVG-Repo, FIGR-8) with held-out splits and distributional statistics, not single-example compression ratios.

Baselines are straw men: BPE is estimated as chars/4 rather than running an actual tokenizer, and none of the cited related systems (StrokeNUWA's VQ-Stroke, LLM4SVG, IconShop-style schemes) are reimplemented or compared, despite README.md:93-98 citing them as the technical foundation. The 'HiVG (Xing et al.)' citation appears misattributed — HiVG is a hierarchical visual-grounding paper, not SVG tokenization — and 'VectorGym (Rodriguez et al.)' is not verifiable, which a reviewer would flag immediately.

The central lossless-compression claim does not survive value-level scrutiny (radius/spacing/count distortions demonstrated above), so the paper-shaped contribution would need to be reframed as lossy rate-distortion: tokens-per-image vs reconstruction error curves against uniform quantization and text baselines. No such curve exists; fidelity is only measured for coordinates that pass through ARCS, not for the L2/L3 scalar-encoding paths where the real loss occurs.

Training results are toy-scale and uncontrolled: a 1.79M-parameter decoder trained on 200 synthetic samples for 10 epochs (8.5s) reaching 35.6% next-token accuracy and 53.3% 'valid SVG' (RESEARCH_SUMMARY.md:73-77) supports no claim about the tokenization helping generation. There is no matched-compute comparison against a char/BPE-tokenized model on the same data, no rendering-based metric (raster IoU, LPIPS, CLIP score), and the HMN-init convergence benefit is asserted but never ablated against Xavier init on the actual training task.

SVG coverage is too narrow to claim 'vector graphics tokenization': no transforms, gradients, text, use/defs, clip paths, stroke styling, fill rules, or non-square/offset viewBoxes (coordinates outside [0, canvas] are silently clamped, arcs.py:194-196; canvas assumed square at ARCS construction, arcs.py:83). Any icon set hit with these features (most of them) would be silently corrupted, so the method cannot be evaluated on real corpora without substantial new engineering.

The adaptive-quantization-vs-learnability tension is unexamined: because the quadtree is rebuilt per input, identical geometry yields different token sequences across images, fragmenting the coordinate distribution a model must learn. A top-venue submission would need an ablation (adaptive vs fixed-grid vs learned VQ codebook) measuring downstream perplexity/generation quality, which is absent.

Verification infrastructure is below publication bar: tests are bespoke print-and-count scripts rather than pytest (each file maintains its own pass/fail counters, e.g. tests/test_fidelity.py:29-39), there is no CI, no property-based or fuzz testing of the parser/detokenizer, and the coverage gaps align exactly with the discovered bugs (REPEAT_N, reserved-ID decoding, value-level round-trip). The '180 assertions' claim counts these script checks, several of which are unconditionally-true placeholders (test_roundtrip.py:263 sets results['arcs_adaptive'] = True regardless of outcome).

summary: GPL Tokenizer is a geometry-aware SVG tokenization pipeline: parser/ converts SVG into a uniform PathCommand IR, analyzer/ extracts differential-geometric and spatial structure, and downstream modules (tokenizer/, embedding/, training/) compress it into 3 token levels and train a small transformer. Concretely: parser/path_parser.py (330 lines) regex-tokenizes the path `d` grammar — all 10 commands (M/L/H/V/C/S/Q/T/A/Z), relative forms, implicit lineto after moveto (path_parser.py:151-154), S/T control-point reflection (256-307), and resolves everything to absolute coordinates with per-command start/end points. parser/svg_parser.py (386 lines) walks the XML via ElementTree and supports exactly 7 element types (path, circle, rect, ellipse, line, polygon, polyline) plus <g> traversal (svg_parser.py:122-136), normalizing basic shapes to path commands (circle/ellipse as 4 kappa-cubics at lines 322-373, rounded rect as lines+arcs at 267-320). analyzer/curvature.py samples curvature at 30 points per segment using exact Bezier derivatives from utils/math_utils.py; analyzer/continuity.py classifies junctions as DISCONTINUOUS/G0/G1/G2 with thresholds centralized in utils/constants.py (with an optional relative-G2 mode). analyzer/shape_detector.py recognizes 4 shapes by per-subpath command-signature matching: M+4C+Z to circle/ellipse (endpoint-only geometric verification, lines 142-260), M+3-4L+Z to rect (perpendicularity dot-product + opposite-side checks, 264-361), and a count-based round-rect heuristic (365-446). analyzer/spatial_analyzer.py detects 7 relation types (H/V center alignment, H/V equal spacing within aligned groups of >=3, axis-reflection symmetry about the global center midlines, equal bbox size) using absolute pixel tolerances of 3-5 px. README.md and RESEARCH_SUMMARY.md claim 2-3x token efficiency vs BPE, 5.6x circle compression with "zero information loss", up to 15x for repeated layouts, 138/138 passing tests, and a toy training run (1.79M params, 200 synthetic samples, 53.3% valid-SVG generation). Runtime probing confirms the pipeline works well on clean axis-aligned synthetic input but breaks (often silently) on transforms, defs/clipPath, compact arc-flag syntax, styled fills, rotated shapes, and non-canonical circle encodings, and the headline baselines/claims are weaker than stated (BPE baseline is len(text)/4, not a real tokenizer; "zero information loss" is falsified by several confirmed cases).
strengths: Path d-grammar coverage is genuinely solid: all 10 command types incl. relative forms, implicit lineto after M (parser/path_parser.py:143-163), S/T smooth-command reflection with correct last-control-point tracking (path_parser.py:256-307), and scientific-notation numbers (path_parser.py:104-106). The S->C and T->Q promotion after resolution gives downstream analyzers a small closed command set.

Clean intermediate representation: every command carries absolute params plus start/end points after resolve_to_absolute() (path_parser.py:184-330), and all 7 supported element types are normalized into the same PathCommand IR (svg_parser.py:250-373), so curvature/continuity/shape analysis is written once. Circle/ellipse normalization uses the correct kappa=0.5522847498 4-cubic construction (svg_parser.py:322-373).

Curvature analysis uses exact analytic Bezier derivatives (utils/math_utils.py deriv1/deriv2 + kappa = |x'y''-y'x''|/|v|^3) sampled at 30 points rather than finite differencing, and quadratic arc length is computed via correct degree elevation to cubic (analyzer/curvature.py:144-148). Degenerate-speed handling exists (constants.degenerate_speed_cubed).

Continuity thresholds are centralized in a frozen GeometricConstants dataclass with documented rationale per threshold and an optional relative-G2 mode to avoid over-sensitivity near kappa~0 (utils/constants.py; analyzer/continuity.py:51-74,160-168) - this fixed a real prior inconsistency (0.1 vs 0.05 G1 cutoffs) and the explicit-arg-overrides-constants API is sensible.

Continuity analysis is subpath-aware: junctions spanning a MOVE are correctly skipped (analyzer/continuity.py:99-102), and shape detection operates per closed M..Z subpath (analyzer/shape_detector.py:126-138), so multi-subpath paths don't produce garbage junctions.

The rect detector does real geometric verification, not just signature matching: normalized dot products for perpendicularity at all 4 corners and opposite-side length equality (analyzer/shape_detector.py:316-341), with degenerate-edge rejection (length < 0.1, lines 330-331). It correctly accepts rotated rectangles as rectangles (though see the params weakness).

The circle/ellipse detector has a sensible two-estimate center consistency check (midpoints of both diagonals must agree, shape_detector.py:188-198) and handles both axis-orderings of the 4 extreme points plus a distance-spread fallback (212-230), so it is robust to the start point being at any of the 4 compass points.

Spatial relation detection is simple but coherent: equal spacing is only sought inside already-center-aligned groups of >=3 (analyzer/spatial_analyzer.py:148-196), symmetry requires all elements to participate before reporting (250-252, avoiding spurious partial claims on its own terms), and grouping is O(n log n) sort-based.

There is a real automated test suite (8 test files, ~1,672 lines; tests/test_roundtrip.py, test_level2.py, test_level3.py etc.) and the v0.5.1 changelog shows responsiveness to prior critique: pixel-unit fidelity APIs with an analytic quantization error bound, stricter generator validation, documented reserved vocabulary ID ranges (README.md:59-69).
weaknesses: Transforms are completely unhandled - the single biggest SVG coverage gap. The transform attribute is stored but never parsed or applied (svg_parser.py:24 comment '미처리', svg_parser.py:141), and a <g transform> is not even propagated to children (confirmed at runtime: <g transform="translate(100,100)"><rect/></g> yields bbox (0,0,10,10) and elem.transform=None). Every downstream coordinate, shape detection, and spatial relation is silently wrong for transformed content, which dominates real-world (Figma/Illustrator-exported) SVGs.

defs/clipPath/mask content leaks in as visible geometry: _collect_elements recurses into children of any unrecognized container (svg_parser.py:150-152). Confirmed: <defs><rect/></defs> and <clipPath><circle/></clipPath> both produce regular elements in doc.elements. Invisible definitions are tokenized as if drawn.

Unsupported-and-silently-dropped features: text/tspan, use/symbol, image, linearGradient/radialGradient, pattern, mask, filter, marker, <style> CSS, nested <svg>, foreignObject - the whitelist is 7 tags (svg_parser.py:123-136). There is no warning or error; documents simply lose content.

All paint/style information is discarded in round-trip: fill/stroke/opacity are collected as raw strings (svg_parser.py:143-147) but never tokenized, and the detokenizer hardcodes fill="none" stroke="black" stroke-width="1" on every output element (tokenizer/detokenizer.py:159-164 and ~15 other sites). The style attribute and CSS classes are never parsed at all. The README's 'zero information loss' (README.md:37) holds only for bare geometry.

Valid SVG arc syntax silently destroys data: compact flag notation 'A5 5 0 0110 10' (legal per the SVG BNF, where flags need no separators) is tokenized by the generic number regex (path_parser.py:104-106) into 6 numbers, which fails the 'i + param_count <= len(params)' loop guard (path_parser.py:147) and drops the entire arc. Confirmed at runtime: only the M survives. Real minified SVGs use this notation heavily.

Arc curvature/tangent analysis is a stub that poisons continuity results: kappa is approximated as 1/mean(rx,ry) ignoring x-rotation and the position-varying curvature of ellipses (analyzer/curvature.py:198-203), arc_length is chord * 1.2 - a magic constant (curvature.py:221) - and both tangent angles are set to the chord direction (curvature.py:209-220). Any G1/G2 judgment at a junction involving an arc (continuity.py:133-156) is wrong by construction; arcs also always report positive kappa so sweep direction is lost and S-shaped arc junctions can falsely pass G2.

Circle detection verifies only segment endpoints, never control points: a 4-petal blob whose four cubic endpoints lie at N/E/S/W of a circle is classified CIRCLE with confidence 1.0 (confirmed at runtime; analyzer/shape_detector.py:166-260 uses only end_point values). Level-2 round-trip then reconstructs a circle in place of the blob - silent geometric corruption directly contradicting the lossless-compression claim.

Rotated rectangles are detected but reconstructed wrong: the perpendicularity check correctly accepts a 45-degree square, but params are the axis-aligned bounding box (shape_detector.py:343-359). Confirmed: M100,50 L150,100 L100,150 L50,100 Z returns RECT {x:50,y:50,width:100,height:100} - a different shape with 2x the area and no rotation.

Common circle encodings are not detected: the two-arc form 'M..A..A..Z' (arguably the most common hand-written/minified circle) returns no detection (confirmed), as do circles approximated with >4 cubics or rotated ellipses. Only the exact M+4C+Z signature is considered (shape_detector.py:156-164), i.e., largely the encoding this same package's own svg_parser produces - the detector is tuned to its own normalizer.

Round-rect detection is a counting heuristic: exactly 4 curve commands and >=3 line commands (shape_detector.py:385-388), corner radii estimated as the mean |dx|,|dy| across curve segments (426-427), hardcoded confidence 0.85 (445). No verification that curves sit at corners or that lines are axis-aligned; many non-round-rect paths match, and reconstruction from bbox + averaged radii is lossy.

Spatial tolerances are absolute pixels (3-5 px defaults, spatial_analyzer.py:69-84) with no viewBox normalization. Confirmed degenerate behavior: a scene 0.3 units wide reports every relation type simultaneously (ALIGN_CENTER_H and _V on the same 4 distinct-x elements, EQUAL_SPACE both axes, both symmetries, EQUAL_SIZE). Conversely a 10,000-unit viewBox would detect nothing. Results are not scale-invariant.

Symmetry detection is shallow: only the two axis-aligned midlines of the centers' bounding box are ever tested (spatial_analyzer.py:208-229); matching compares centers and bbox width/height only (282-289), so a mirrored asymmetric glyph pair (b vs d shapes) counts as symmetric without any geometry comparison; no diagonal, rotational, or partial symmetry; all-or-nothing participation (line 250) means one outlier kills detection.

Grouping logic has correctness edges: _group_by_value chains against the first element of the group (spatial_analyzer.py:342), causing drift and order-dependence at tolerance boundaries; equal-size grouping is greedy and non-transitive (300-323); each element belongs to at most one alignment group, so overlapping patterns are missed. EQUAL_SIZE uses bbox dims only, so a circle and a square of equal bbox are 'equal size' (312-313).

Bounding boxes everywhere use only command endpoints, not control points or curve extrema (svg_parser.py:29-39; tokenizer/spatial_tokenizer.py:131-137), despite BezierMath.bounding_box_cubic existing (math_utils.py:177). Curves bulging past their endpoints corrupt centers/sizes fed to the spatial analyzer.

Minor parser robustness gaps: namespace handling is regex deletion of the xmlns declaration (svg_parser.py:79-80) so prefixed documents (<svg:path>) break; polygon points regex '[+-]?[\d.]+' (svg_parser.py:216) rejects exponent notation and mis-tokenizes '1.2.3'; _parse_length ignores units entirely - '50%', '10mm', '2em' all become bare numbers (svg_parser.py:375-379); H/V-only rects: a rect drawn as M+H+V+H+Z works, but the 3-vertex CLOSE inference assumes the missing vertex equals the start (shape_detector.py:302-310) without verifying perpendicular closure.
research_limits: No real-world evaluation data at all: every reported number comes from self-generated synthetic SVGs (training/generator.py, 200 samples, 7 shape types). No standard corpus (FIGR-8-SVG, SVG-Stack, DeepSVG icons dataset, noto-emoji, Material icons) is ever parsed, and given the confirmed transform/defs/paint gaps, the pipeline would fail or silently corrupt most files in those corpora. A top-venue paper needs parse-success and fidelity rates on a real distribution.

The headline '2-3x better than BPE' baseline is fake-BPE: estimated token count = len(svg_text)/4.0 (tests/test_roundtrip.py:331-333), never an actual tokenizer (tiktoken, SentencePiece, Llama/GPT vocab). All compression ratios (2-3x, 5.6x, 15x in README.md:35-39) inherit this proxy. Reviewers will run tiktoken in five minutes and get different numbers.

The central 'zero information loss' claim (README.md:37, RESEARCH_SUMMARY.md:60) is falsified by construction in at least four confirmed ways: paint/style dropped, transforms ignored, rotated rect replaced by its axis-aligned bbox, and non-circular blobs replaced by circles (confidence 1.0). There is no rendering-based fidelity metric (raster MSE/SSIM/LPIPS/IoU) anywhere; fidelity is measured only on coordinates of commands that survived tokenization - errors of omission are invisible to the metric.

Shape detection and spatial relation detection have no measured precision/recall: there is no labeled evaluation set, no false-positive analysis (the blob-as-circle case shows FP rate is nonzero), and confidence scores are hardcoded constants (1.0, 0.85) or a single-distance formula (shape_detector.py:238) - not calibrated probabilities. Tolerances (3-5 px) are hand-set with no sensitivity study and are not scale-invariant.

No comparison to the cited prior work: HiVG, StrokeNUWA, LLM4SVG, VectorGym are listed as 'technical foundation' (README.md:93-98) but never compared against, empirically or qualitatively; at least one citation (VectorGym, 'Rodriguez et al.') is difficult to verify as a real publication. A venue reviewer will demand head-to-head token-efficiency and generation-quality numbers against StrokeNUWA/IconShop/DeepSVG-style baselines.

Downstream-model evidence is a toy: 1.79M-parameter transformer, 200 samples, 10 epochs, 8.5 seconds of training, 53.3% valid-SVG rate (RESEARCH_SUMMARY.md:73-77) with no control condition - no char-level or BPE-tokenized model at matched compute/data to show the tokenization itself causes the gain. The HMN-init claim (0.52 vs 0.00 cosine similarity) is a property of the construction, not a demonstrated training benefit; no ablation isolates any component.

The spatial-relation vocabulary covers only axis-aligned phenomena (7 relation types, all H/V), so the 'Level 3 spatial intelligence' contribution cannot represent grids, radial/rotational layouts, diagonal alignment, or scaled repetition - the patterns that make real designs compressible. The claimed 15x compression applies to a single hand-picked case (5 identical circles in a row).

Evaluation circularity: the shape detector primarily recognizes the exact 4-cubic encodings that this package's own svg_parser emits for <circle>/<ellipse>, and tests feed parser output back into the detector. The 138/138 passing tests validate internal consistency, not generality; trivial adversarial inputs that fail today (compact arc flags, unit lengths, two-arc circles, transformed groups) are absent from the suite.

Engineering hygiene that blocks reproducibility/release: the editable install exposes top-level packages named parser, utils, tests, tokenizer (egg finder mapping), which shadow common names and break 'import analyzer' due to beyond-top-level relative imports (confirmed ImportError); the package is unpublishable as an artifact without restructuring under a single gpl_tokenizer namespace. License is proprietary (README.md:102), precluding the artifact/code release most venues now expect.

Synthetic-only, self-referential data: the model is trained AND evaluated on sequences emitted by the same hand-written grammar (SyntheticSVGGenerator, training/synthetic_dataset.py:39-283; 7 shape categories, 200 samples). There is no real-world SVG corpus (e.g. FIGR-8-SVG, icon sets), no held-out distribution shift, and therefore zero evidence of generalization. The model is at best learning back the generator's grammar.

No baseline comparison for the central claim: nothing compares GPL tokenization to an actual alternative tokenization (BPE/char-level) with the same downstream model at equal compute, and nothing compares against prior SVG generative models (DeepSVG, IconShop, StrokeNUWA, LLM4SVG). The 'BPE' numbers in compression claims are character-count heuristics: tests/test_level2.py:252 (bpe_est = len(svg_text)//4) and tests/test_level3.py:363-366 (bpe_tokens = avg_chars/3). No tiktoken/HF tokenizer appears anywhere in the repo.

The core contribution (HMN initialization) has no outcome ablation: hmn_init.py:13 claims convergence acceleration ('수렴 가속'), and use_hmn_init=False exists (gpl_embedding.py:182), but no experiment anywhere trains HMN vs random init and compares loss curves or generation quality. The only HMN evidence is that the init has the intended geometric structure before training (tests/test_embedding.py:222-254), which says nothing about whether it helps.

Evaluation metrics are not credible: I empirically verified that garbage sequences ([BOS] + 10 random coordinate tokens + [EOS]) score structural=1.000 and geometric=1.000 on GPLEvaluator, while ground-truth training data scores 0.987/0.995 (penalized because evaluator.py:112-117 includes CLOSE=17 in cmd_tokens and demands a coordinate after it). The headline '0.88 structural / 0.99 geometric' results (RESEARCH_SUMMARY.md:77) are therefore close to meaningless. No rendering-based metric (rasterize + FID/CLIPScore/LPIPS), no human eval, no reconstruction-vs-target comparison for generation.

Statistically insufficient experiments: headline numbers come from a single un-seeded training run inside a test script (tests/test_training.py:166-191: 200 samples, 10 epochs) and generation rates from n=30 samples (tests/test_training.py:266), giving roughly +/-18pt confidence interval on the 53.3% valid-SVG rate. No repeated runs, no variance, no significance testing.

Toy scale with no scaling evidence: 1.79M params with 40% in the tied embedding and 14.7% dead cross-attention weight; max_seq_len 64-128; no experiment shows the tokenization benefit persists at a scale anyone would publish, and no integration with a pretrained LLM despite the README pitch being about LLMs.

Citation integrity problems: README.md:93-98 and RESEARCH_SUMMARY.md:128-135 cite 'HiVG (Xing et al.) - Hierarchical SVG tokenization' (HiVG is a visual-grounding paper, not SVG tokenization) and 'VectorGym (Rodriguez et al.)' (not a known benchmark; possibly confused with VGBench). A reviewer checking related work would flag this immediately, and there is no positioning against the directly comparable DeepSVG/IconShop line of work.

Overstated claims vs implementation: README.md:37 says '5.6x compression with zero information loss' while the same README (line 64) documents quantization error of ~2.6px (adaptive) to ~49px (default) - the round-trip is lossy by construction (ARCS cell quantization, tokenizer/arcs.py:185-226). 'Up to 15x fewer tokens' rests on the heuristic BPE estimate above. The text-conditional generation use case implied by the README (design tools, text-to-SVG) does not exist; only unconditional and 2-token shape-prefix generation is implemented (training/generator.py:59-96).
strengths: Headline engineering numbers are honest and reproduce: I verified vocab_size=5,561 and total params=1,794,320 (1.79M) empirically by instantiating GPLTransformer with the test config; embedding=736,016 matches the v0.4 '736K' claim, and weight tying (gpl_transformer.py:115) is real and tested (tests/test_training.py:145).

HMN initialization does what it locally claims: the sinusoidal quadtree encoding (hmn_init.py:203-276) measurably produces ~0.52 cosine similarity for adjacent coordinate tokens vs ~0 for random init, near>far similarity ordering, level-dependent norms, and semantic clustering of commands/shapes - all verified in tests/test_embedding.py:104-157 and 222-254. The docstring derivation (hmn_init.py:17-55) is mathematically careful and explicitly disclaims 0.52 as a design artifact rather than a target - unusually honest documentation.

Sound core tokenization design: a coherent 3-level scheme (primitive commands -> composite shapes -> spatial relations) with a documented, extensible vocabulary layout including reserved ID ranges (tokenizer/vocabulary.py:106-126), bidirectional coord<->id maps, and a quadtree ARCS quantizer with an analytic error bound (theoretical_max_error, roundtrip_fidelity at tokenizer/arcs.py:252-311) plus pixel-unit fidelity measurement (detokenizer.measure_fidelity).

The training pipeline is genuinely end-to-end and runs on CPU in seconds: dataset -> collator with correct shift-by-one next-token targets and padding masks (synthetic_dataset.py:334-365) -> pre-LN decoder with causal mask and key-padding mask -> AdamW + cosine LR + grad clipping + checkpointing + early stopping (trainer.py) -> autoregressive sampling with top-k/top-p (correctly implemented unsort via scatter, gpl_transformer.py:269-281) -> detokenization -> validation.

v0.5.1 hardening shows real self-criticism: generator._validate_svg (training/generator.py:186-215) was upgraded from a 'starts with M' heuristic to actual PathParser parsing requiring >=1 renderable command, geometric thresholds were centralized after a documented inconsistency, and the docstrings candidly record the prior weaknesses.

Type-aware embedding architecture is a reasonable inductive-bias design: token embedding + token-type embedding + a coordinate-structure MLP fed by an exact (level, nx, ny) lookup table (gpl_embedding.py:82-154), so spatial information reaches the model through a continuous channel independent of the learned embedding.
summary: GPL Tokenizer is a ~6,600-line Python research prototype implementing a geometry-aware tokenization scheme for SVG plus a small end-to-end training pipeline. The tokenizer side (parser/, analyzer/, tokenizer/) converts SVG (path, circle, rect, ellipse, line, polygon, polyline) into a 5,561-token vocabulary: 8 command tokens, 4 composite-shape tokens, 4 continuity tokens (G0-G2), 16 curvature bins, 11 spatial-relation tokens, and 5,461 quadtree 'ARCS' coordinate tokens (levels 0-6, tokenizer/vocabulary.py:134-153), with a detokenizer reconstructing SVG. The ML side: embedding/hmn_init.py overwrites Xavier-initialized embedding rows with structured vectors - coordinate tokens get an L2-normalized 2D sinusoidal encoding of their quadtree cell center scaled by 0.8^level (hmn_init.py:203-276), command/shape/spatial tokens get seeded cluster vectors, continuity/curvature tokens get ordered offsets along a fixed direction. embedding/gpl_embedding.py combines this token embedding with a 7-class type embedding, a coordinate-structure MLP over an exact (level, nx, ny) lookup table, sinusoidal positional encoding, and a projection. training/gpl_transformer.py wraps this in a 4-layer, d_model=128 decoder built from nn.TransformerDecoder with a dummy all-zeros memory and a weight-tied LM head - 1,794,320 params (I verified this empirically; the 1.79M claim is accurate, but 264,192 of those params are cross-attention attending to a zero vector, i.e. dead weight). training/synthetic_dataset.py generates training token sequences directly from a hand-coded grammar (7 categories: circle/rect/ellipse/line-path/curve-path/mixed/multi) without ever touching the SVG parser; trainer.py is a standard AdamW + cosine-anneal loop; generator.py samples autoregressively and detokenizes; evaluator.py computes five heuristic quality scores. Claimed results (loss 7.81->2.91 in 10 epochs on 200 samples, 53.3% valid SVG, 0.88 structural / 0.99 geometric scores, 2-3x GID vs BPE, up to 15x compression) all come from script-style test files, and several rest on weak measurement: the 'BPE' baseline is a character-count heuristic (len/4 or len/3, tests/test_level2.py:252, tests/test_level3.py:363-366), and I empirically showed the evaluator awards perfect 1.000 structural and geometric scores to random-garbage token sequences while ground-truth data scores 0.987/0.995. The work is a competently engineered prototype with genuinely well-documented init math, but it is several major experiments away from a publishable ML paper.
weaknesses: Evaluation metrics are trivially gameable - verified empirically: sequences of [BOS] + random coordinate tokens + [EOS] score structural=1.000 and geometric=1.000, while ground-truth synthetic data scores 0.987/0.995. Root causes: _structural_score only checks BOS/EOS presence, command-followed-by-coord, and no-interior-PAD (evaluator.py:85-125); a sequence with no commands skips all command checks. Worse, cmd_tokens includes CLOSE=17 (evaluator.py:112), so valid CLOSE->EOS endings are penalized - the evaluator scores ground truth below garbage. The docstring-promised 'Token Accuracy' metric (evaluator.py:8) is never implemented, and _geometric_score's claimed 'coordinate range check' (evaluator.py:131) does not exist in the code.

Baseline for all compression claims is fake BPE: tests/test_level2.py:252 uses bpe_est = len(svg_text)//4 and tests/test_level3.py:363-366 uses avg_chars/3. No real tokenizer (tiktoken, HF) is ever run, yet README.md:35-39 presents '2-3x more efficient than standard text tokenization' and 'up to 15x fewer tokens' as key results.

Architectural defect in the transformer: gpl_transformer.py:172 feeds nn.TransformerDecoder a dummy all-zeros memory tensor. Cross-attention over a single zero vector can only produce a constant offset, so 264,192 params (14.7% of the 1.79M model) are wasted; the correct construction is a TransformerEncoder with a causal mask. The '1.79M param' model is effectively ~1.53M.

Training-data/decoder convention mismatch for circles: synthetic_dataset.py:95 encodes radius as coord_to_id(level, r, 0) ('radius encoded in qx'), but the real CompositeTokenizer encodes (r, r) in canvas space (composite_tokenizer.py:164-165) and the Detokenizer decodes r = (radius_x + radius_y)/2 (detokenizer.py:509). A model trained on the synthetic distribution and decoded with the shipped Detokenizer systematically produces wrong radii (roughly halved, plus cell-center offset). The synthetic generator also emits raw grid indices while the real tokenizer quantizes canvas-space pixels - two incompatible coordinate conventions in one codebase.

Canvas mismatch in generation: ARCS dequantizes into a 300x300 canvas by default (arcs.py:78) but generator._wrap_svg hardcodes viewBox 0 0 256 256 (generator.py:176-184), so generated geometry near the right/bottom edges is silently clipped.

Trainer config promises features that do not exist: trainer.py:92 docstring says 'linear warmup + cosine decay' but warmup_steps (trainer.py:36) is never read and the scheduler is plain CosineAnnealingLR; label_smoothing (trainer.py:41) is also never used (compute_loss at gpl_transformer.py:203 passes only ignore_index).

Latent copy-paste bug: synthetic_dataset.py:69 computes idy = coord_to_id(level, qy, qy) - (qy, qy) instead of a y-encoding. The method _coord_id_at is currently dead code, but it is a landmine for anyone extending the generator.

HMN init side effects untested: coordinate tokens are given norm ~1.0 vectors while special tokens (BOS/EOS/SEP/UNK) keep tiny Xavier values (~0.03 scale) and PAD is zeroed (hmn_init.py:98-102, 246-250). With weight tying, initial logits are systematically biased toward high-norm coordinate tokens and against EOS - plausibly degrading early generation behavior - and no test or experiment examines this interaction. Weight tying itself is conceptually shaky here because the input embedding is consumed pre-projection concatenated with type/coord features (gpl_embedding.py:270-271), so the decoder output space is not the token embedding space.

Tests are print-and-count scripts, not assertions: all 8 test files use a custom check() that increments global counters and prints check/cross marks (e.g. tests/test_training.py:46-53), with module-level execution and sys.exit. Under pytest these do not register as test cases; failures surface only via exit code. The '138/180 tests' framing in RESEARCH_SUMMARY.md:115-124 counts these prints.

Narrow SVG coverage for a 'tokenize any SVG' pitch: transform attributes are captured but explicitly unprocessed (svg_parser.py:24 - '미처리, 추후 확장'); no <g> transform inheritance, no text, gradients, CSS styles, clip paths, or use/defs; styling attributes are stored but dropped from tokenization, and the detokenizer hardcodes fill=none stroke=black (detokenizer.py:510-511). Spatial L3 only covers axis-aligned alignment/reflection/equal-spacing - no rotation, grids, or radial symmetry (vocabulary.py:51-72).
